newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips snap record run, post small losses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips snap record run, post small losses.

text.p: U.S. blue chips snapped a six session run of record closing highs on Monday, posting a small loss ahead of a report on May retail inflation.
In generally subdued trading, the Dow industrials finished down unofficially 10 points, or 0.13 percent, at 7772.
In the previous six sessions, the blue chip average had shot up 477 points, or 6.5 percent.
"Even God rested on the seventh day," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates.
But whatever profit-taking there was in blue chips did not spread to the broader market.

The strongest of the major indexes was the Nasdaq composite, which rose nine points, or 0.6 percent, to 1432, its second record close in a row. Buying in high technology stocks, which had lagged the recent rally in blue chips, lifted Nasdaq, traders said.

"You're seeing a rally in the big-cap high tech names," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co. Among them, Intel Corp rose 2-1/2 to 147-1/4 and Microsoft Corp added 1-3/4 to 131-3/8.
The Standard & Poor's 500 index managed a gain of about a point to 894, its seventh consecutive close at an all-time high.

Some investors chose to take some profits ahead of Tuesday's report on the May Consumer Price Index. But after last week's report of soft retail sales and producer prices, there was little concern that the CPI would show inflationary pressures, analysts said.
"The PPI number last week put a lot of people at ease," White said. "The retail sales numbers have put a lot of people at ease."

Some of that confidence was shown in the inflation-sensitive bond market, where the 30-year Treasury bond was up 14/32 in late trading, its yield dropping to 6.69 percent from Friday's close at 6.73 percent.
Market players said they expected news on corporate profits to be the focus for Wall Street in the coming weeks.

Given the recent rally, investors will likely be quick to dump stocks in companies giving any indications that their earnings will not meet expectations. "Shoot first and ask questions later, that's going to be the modus operandi," said Guy Truicko, equity portfolio manager at Unity Management.

Dell Computer Corp vice chairman Mort Topfer said in an interview the company's momentum remains strong and the company is "very pleased" with the current quarter and the momentum in the direct PC business. The computer maker's shares rose 4-1/4 to 115-3/8. Compaq Computer Corp shared in the rally, rising five to 105-1/4.

Merrill Lynch downgraded its near-term ratings on several health maintenance organization companies. Among them, Aetna Inc fell 3-1/4 to 109-1/2, United HealthCare Corp dropped 2-1/4 to 54-1/8 and WellPoint Health Networks Inc dipped 1-7/8 to 48-7/8.

Shares in Italian apparel and footware company Fila Holdings SpA tumbled 4-1/2 to 32-7/8 on the New York Stock Exchange, clipped by a company forecast that second-quarter earnings would be below analysts' expectations.
Anchor Gaming jumped 2-3/8 to 40 after saying that, based on preliminary internal financial reports for April and May, analysts' estimates for its current quarterly profits may be "conservative."
The S&P 500 index rose 0.63 of a point to 893.90, a record. The Nasdaq Composite rose 8.92 points to 1431.95, a record.
